name: MD-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+10 district with a Democratic incumbent seeking re-election
Roughly 40-to-1 fundraising advantage for Olszewski ($1.24M vs $29k)
Prediction markets price the Democrat near 95%
No public polling or expert ratings; outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: A D+10 incumbent seat, a roughly forty-to-one fundraising edge, and market pricing near 95% for the Democrat all point the same direction, and no polling or outside spending suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Fresh polling, significant outside spending against Olszewski, or a strongly Republican national environment could narrow what is otherwise a lopsided margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 2nd District leans Democratic by about ten points, and first-term incumbent Johnny Olszewski is seeking re-election with the advantages of incumbency and a dominant financial position. He has raised roughly $1.24 million and holds about $644,000 on hand, while Republican Dave Wallace has raised about $29,000 with roughly $7,000 available. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent, and prediction markets put his winning chances near 95%.

No public general-election polling is available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing. Everything points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the incumbent favored by roughly twenty points. The main sources of uncertainty are the absence of polling and the possibility of a sharply favorable Republican national environment, but neither appears close to erasing a gap of this size.
